title: Australia captain Mitchell Marsh suffers testicular bleeding after training ground accident
content:
Australia captain Mitchell Marsh was ruled out of his side’s opening match against Ireland at the Men’s T20 World Cup after suffering internal testicular bleeding in a training ground accident.

Marsh, 34, was struck in the groin by a ball in training earlier this week. He did his pre-match captain’s press conference as scheduled but was not named in the team to take on Ireland on Tuesday.

Steve Smith, Australia’s standby player, has been called up as cover for Marsh and is now travelling to Sri Lanka to acclimatise.

A statement from Cricket Australia confirmed: “He is experiencing ongoing pain and discomfort which is restricting his movement.

“Scans have confirmed internal testicular bleeding, and he will require a period of rest and rehabilitation. His return to play will be guided by symptom resolution and medical advice.”

Marsh is one of Australia’s most experienced T20 players, having played 83 internationals and scored 2,102 runs. He has also taken 17 wickets.

Smith, 36, has not played a T20 international since February 2024.

Australia’s preparations for the T20 World Cup have already been hit by injuries to fast bowlers Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins, who were both ruled out of the tournament.

Travis Head captained Australia in Marsh’s absence against Ireland, and was run out for six in the second over.
